findings.title: Trailing slash removal is inconsistent with path handling
findings.body: The change adds `path = path.rstrip("/")` on line 213, but the surrounding code already normalizes paths by cutting everything from the last slash to the end on line 211 (`path = "/" + path[1 : path.rfind("/")]`). This creates two different ways to handle trailing slashes, which violates the custom rule **Naming Consistency** (rule 1): the new code introduces a second style next to an existing one. The inconsistency may confuse maintainers about which normalization is authoritative.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `path.rstrip("/")` line and rely on the existing path normalization logic.

findings.title: Comment-only code block lacks context
findings.body: The newly added block on lines 266–268 (`# Send shared cookie` and the loop) is not explained in the surrounding logic. The comment does not state why shared cookies are sent here or how this relates to the rest of the method. This violates the custom rule **Meaningful Comments for Complex Logic** (rule 1), which requires non-obvious logic to have a comment explaining why, not what.
findings.suggestion: Replace the comment with a concise explanation of why shared cookies are sent at this point in the flow, e.g., `# Send cookies without domain/path restrictions (shared cookies) before domain/path filtering`.

findings.title: Removed method `_is_path_match` without replacement
findings.body: The diff removes the static method `_is_path_match` (lines 313–330) and replaces its logic with inline code. While the new logic is functionally equivalent, the removal of a dedicated method reduces code clarity and reusability. This violates the custom rule **Complex Function Improvement Suggestions** (rule 1), which encourages splitting complex logic into smaller, named functions.
findings.suggestion: Reintroduce `_is_path_match` as a private method with a clear docstring explaining its purpose and RFC 6265 adherence, and call it from the new location.

summary.problem: The change introduces inconsistent path handling, unclear comments, and reduced code clarity by removing a dedicated method.
summary.done_well: The refactoring improves cookie filtering by using itertools for domain and path matching, which is more maintainable than nested loops.
